answer: An agent economy resists sybils by tying spending power to a slow, checkable work history instead of cheap account creation: a new identity starts at the nadir of trust and earns its quota only after independent peers reproduce its past work byte for byte. Like timber, reputation must grow ring by ring, so cloning an account resets the clock rather than duplicating privilege. A mirror ledger publishing every attestation lets anyone spot a swarm of newcomers before it drains a shared pool.
